comparison: Perfect agreement on MD simulation data (C24-C27, C64-C67). Both evaluations find the computational work sound and accept that simulations demonstrate induced-fit mechanism and substrate-dependent conformational stabilization.

Disagreement on conformational change claims (C29-C30, C55-C57). OpenEval considers the ratchet mechanism hypothetical and requiring validation, while peer reviewers accept the structural observations and mechanistic interpretations without challenge.

Strong agreement on biochemical validation (C4, C21-C23). Both evaluations accept the primer extension assays demonstrating differential RNA vs DNA activity and the clever experimental design using dG-rich sequences to support A-form recognition mechanism.

Significant disagreement on synthesis termination mechanism (C5, C34-C35, C54). OpenEval finds the ~10 nucleotide limit well-supported by structural and biochemical data, while peer reviewers express confusion about contradictory literature stating ~20 nt synthesis, requesting clarification.

Agreement on uncertainty regarding spontaneous release model (C6, C28, C58-C60). Both evaluations find the model plausible but lacking direct experimental evidence for primer release or handoff to Pol δ/ε, requiring additional validation.

Agreement on genomic stability claims being speculative (C7, C39, C61-C62). Both evaluations note the lack of genetic evidence and request that language be adjusted to reflect these are plausible hypotheses rather than demonstrated facts.

Strong agreement on crystallographic data quality (C3, C13-C14, C40-C45). Both evaluations praise the structural work as technically sound and impressive, accepting R-factors, refinement statistics, and overall crystallographic methods. However, peer review R5 questions C13 specifically regarding active catalysis.

Disagreement on claim C13 regarding catalytic incorporation. OpenEval accepts the ternary complex as demonstrating active catalysis, while peer reviewers question whether incorporation occurred before crystallization and request detailed active site geometry comparison.

Agreement on structural analysis of protein-DNA interface (C15-C16, C46-C50). Both evaluations accept the quantitative structural analysis and comparisons to other B-family polymerases as valid and well-supported by crystallographic data.

Agreement on molecular interaction details (C17-C20, C53). Both evaluations accept the specific residue-level interactions observed in the crystal structure as valid structural evidence for RNA primer recognition mechanism.

Disagreement on C51 (protein-protein interaction). OpenEval questions physiological relevance and considers it potentially a crystallographic artifact, while peer reviewers include it among accepted structural observations without specific critique.

OpenEval finds structural interpretation of published mutational data (C31-C32) reasonable. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific claims about Ser1134 and its role in RNA recognition.
OpenEval accepts conceptual comparison to Pol η termination mechanism (C36) as valid comparative analysis. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific comparison.
OpenEval accepts experimental observation of residual activity in mutant (C63) as straightforward result. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific finding.
OpenEval accepts background/context claims (C1-C2, C8-C12) as appropriately cited established knowledge. Peer reviewers do not separately evaluate these contextual claims.
